# gitmoap_repository_fork (Data Source)

Get a repository's fork relationship. Where this fork came from, whether its code belongs to the repositories it was forked from, what its copy brought, how far its tracked branch has drifted as of the last refresh, and what you may do with it. A repository you cannot see is named only as `{"visible": false}`. A repository that is not a fork answers 404 with `NOT_A_FORK`.

The token needs `repo:read`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "gitmoap_repository_by_path" "api" {
  full_path = "acme/platform/api"
}

data "gitmoap_repository_fork" "api" {
  repo_id = data.gitmoap_repository_by_path.api.repository_id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `repo_id` (String) Repository ID

### Read-Only

- `auto_sync` (Attributes) Whether pushes to the upstream branch fast-forward the fork's tracked branch automatically, as whom, and why it stopped if it did. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--auto_sync))
- `bound_to` (Attributes List) The repositories its code belongs to — empty for an independent fork — each as far as you
can see it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--bound_to))
- `code_search_enabled` (Boolean) Whether code search indexes it.
- `copied` (Attributes) What the fork copied from its upstream when it was created. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--copied))
- `created_at` (String) When.
- `created_by` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--created_by))
- `detach_closes_merge_requests` (Number) On a detach preview only: how many open merge requests between this fork and the rest of
its network — from it, and into it from other forks — the detach would close.
- `failure` (Attributes) Why the copy stopped for good. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--failure))
- `kind` (String) `bound`: a fork of private code, or a private fix fork — only people who can read the repositories it is bound to can read it, and it never leaves its upstream's organization. `independent`: a fork of a public or internal repository, whose audience is its own within its visibility ceiling.
- `network` (Attributes) The network a fork belongs to: every repository descended by forking from one root. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--network))
- `pipelines_enabled` (Boolean) Whether its pipelines run.
- `purpose` (String) `fork`: an ordinary fork. `private_fix`: a private fork in which a security fix to its upstream is prepared out of view and landed in one step.
- `relationship` (String) `linked`: the fork can sync from its upstream and propose to it. `detached`: its Owner ended that relationship; it no longer syncs or proposes, and a bound fork stays bound.
- `repository_id` (String)
- `state` (String) `copying`: the upstream's branches and tags are still being copied, and the fork serves nothing yet. `ready`: the copy is complete. `failed`: the copy stopped for good; `failure` says why.
- `tracking` (Attributes) How far the fork's tracked branch is from its upstream branch, as of the last refresh — never computed on a read. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tracking))
- `upstream` (Attributes) The repository a fork was created from, as far as you can see it: `visible: false` names nothing, because the upstream is a repository you cannot see. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--upstream))
- `viewer` (Attributes) What you may do with this fork. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--viewer))
- `visibility_ceiling` (String)

<a id="nestedatt--auto_sync"></a>
### Nested Schema for `auto_sync`

Read-Only:

- `actor` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--auto_sync--actor))
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether it is on.
- `paused_reason` (String) `diverged`: the fork branch has commits the upstream lacks. `refused`: the fork's push rules refused the move. `actor_lost_access`: the person auto-sync runs as can no longer read the upstream, or is gone. `upstream_narrower`: the upstream became less visible than the fork. `privileged_paths`: the upstream's new commits change a pipeline file, the catalog declaration or a CODEOWNERS file, which only a person's sync may bring in.

<a id="nestedatt--auto_sync--actor"></a>
### Nested Schema for `auto_sync.actor`

Read-Only:

- `avatar_url` (String) The principal's picture, when one is known. Absent otherwise: a client derives the
deterministic avatar URL itself.
- `email` (String) The principal's address. An agent's is a generated no-reply address — the author of its
commits. `unknown` on a deleted actor and empty on a redacted one.
- `id` (String) The principal's id: a user id, a service account id or an agent id, as `kind` says. Empty on
a redacted actor.
- `kind` (String) A person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — which of the three a principal is,
and so which page it links to: a person's profile, a service account's page or an agent's page.
- `username` (String) The name to show: a person's or service account's username, or an agent's handle (which
always ends in `-ai`). `deleted-user` when the actor no longer resolves, `redacted` when the
caller may not see who it was. A closed account whose work stays is `closed-` and twelve hex
digits, a shape no open account may take, with an address under `.invalid`.



<a id="nestedatt--bound_to"></a>
### Nested Schema for `bound_to`

Read-Only:

- `deleted` (Boolean) `true` once the upstream has been deleted; the fork stays, and says so.
- `full_path` (String)
- `repository_id` (String)
- `visible` (Boolean) Whether you can see the upstream. When `false`, nothing else about it is named.


<a id="nestedatt--copied"></a>
### Nested Schema for `copied`

Read-Only:

- `branches` (String) `default_branch`: only the upstream's default branch. `all`: every branch.
- `completed_at` (String) When the copy completed.
- `ref_count` (Number) How many refs it copied in all.
- `refs` (Attributes List) Up to a hundred of the refs it copied, with the commit each arrived at. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--copied--refs))
- `tags` (Boolean) Whether it copied tags.

<a id="nestedatt--copied--refs"></a>
### Nested Schema for `copied.refs`

Read-Only:

- `ref` (String) The full ref name.
- `sha` (String) The commit it arrived at.

<a id="nestedatt--failure"></a>
### Nested Schema for `failure`

Read-Only:

- `message` (String) What it means, in words.
- `reason` (String) `authority_revoked`: the person forking could no longer fork the upstream when the copy ran. `upstream_deleted`: the upstream was deleted during the copy. `upstream_narrowed`: the upstream became less visible during the copy — fork it again to be classified afresh. `storage_quota`: the copy would not fit in the destination's storage. `copy_failed`: the copy itself failed.


<a id="nestedatt--network"></a>
### Nested Schema for `network`

Read-Only:

- `depth` (Number) How many forks lie between this one and the root, itself included.
- `id` (String)
- `root` (Attributes) The repository a fork was created from, as far as you can see it: `visible: false` names nothing, because the upstream is a repository you cannot see. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--network--root))

<a id="nestedatt--network--root"></a>
### Nested Schema for `network.root`

Read-Only:

- `deleted` (Boolean) `true` once the upstream has been deleted; the fork stays, and says so.
- `full_path` (String)
- `repository_id` (String)
- `visible` (Boolean) Whether you can see the upstream. When `false`, nothing else about it is named.



<a id="nestedatt--tracking"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tracking`

Read-Only:

- `ahead` (Number) Commits the fork branch has that the upstream branch lacks.
- `as_of` (String) When the counts were taken.
- `behind` (Number) Commits the upstream branch has that the fork branch lacks.
- `branch` (String)
- `sync_available` (Boolean) Whether a sync could run now.
- `sync_unavailable_reason` (String) Why not, when it could not.
- `upstream_branch` (String)
- `upstream_sha` (String) The upstream commit the counts were taken against.


<a id="nestedatt--upstream"></a>
### Nested Schema for `upstream`

Read-Only:

- `deleted` (Boolean) `true` once the upstream has been deleted; the fork stays, and says so.
- `full_path` (String)
- `repository_id` (String)
- `visible` (Boolean) Whether you can see the upstream. When `false`, nothing else about it is named.


<a id="nestedatt--viewer"></a>
### Nested Schema for `viewer`

Read-Only:

- `can_detach` (Boolean) You may detach it from its upstream.
- `can_enable_pipelines` (Boolean) You may turn its pipelines on.
- `can_sync` (Boolean) You may sync it from its upstream.
